_file_metadata.task: Governance Hardening & Post-700 Ownership Transition — Tooling Review
_file_metadata.methodology: Line-level source inspection of 6 tool files + 1 manifest + scanning scripts. Cross-referenced against S725 Governance Detection Standard v1.0 mandatory prohibitions (section 3) and required methodologies (section 4).

overall_summary: 3 of 6 reviewed tools have at least one forbidden methodology instance. The governance guard itself is non-compliant (DL-029-vulnerable +/-1200 char window forward-scan). Two scan scripts use QuestionID-split forward-scan. The ExplanationValidator and two modern scan scripts (s710r, s805) are compliant. The DEFECT_MANIFEST uses mixed methodologies with substantial DL-029 contamination for Packs D/E. Build registry is partially compliant (string-aware but uses eval not Function constructor for cases).

checks.finding: USES FORBIDDEN METHODOLOGY
checks.detail: findDL008Violations() (lines 42-61) uses global regex to find non-empty ExplanationWrong[A-D], then searches a +/-1200 character window around the match for CorrectChoice. This is the exact DL-029-vulnerable pattern prohibited by S725 Detection Standard sections 3.1 and 3.3. For Pack B (CC before QID within object), the window captures the adjacent item CC. S724 explicitly identified this gap.

checks.finding: YES
checks.detail: Global regex iterates all non-empty EW fields. For each match, searches within +/-1200 char window for corresponding CorrectChoice. In Pack B where CC appears ~3-40 lines before QID and EW fields appear after, the window may straddle two objects. S724 explicitly identified this gap (line 284 of Detection Standard).

checks.finding: YES — +/-1200 character window extraction (lines 53-55)
checks.detail: winStart = Math.max(0, pos - 1200); winEnd = Math.min(text.length, pos + 1200); This fixed window either truncates fields in large question objects or spans adjacent items. Results are window-parameter-dependent (violates C6).

checks.finding: NOT APPLICABLE
checks.detail: Guard does not use brace-matching; it operates on raw text via regex. This avoids DL-020 (string-unaware brace counter) but introduces DL-029 (cross-object field attribution) instead.

checks.finding: NONE
checks.detail: No distinction between metadata-block ChoiceA-D and content-block Choices.{A,B,C,D}. The regex captures flat ExplanationWrong[A-D] and searches for flat CorrectChoice. Cannot detect DL-016 (Choice mismatch between blocks) because it operates on raw text without object parsing.

checks.finding: NO
checks.detail: CorrectChoice and ExplanationWrong are matched via independent regex captures within a character window, not extracted from a bounded object. Pairing is by character-proximity (window), not object membership. This is exactly the Incorrect pattern described in Detection Standard section 4.3.

gaps_found: GAP-R2-01: DL-008 detection uses regex window-based forward-scan (DL-029 vulnerable)
GAP-R2-02: No Function constructor parse or object-bounded extraction
GAP-R2-03: Window size hardcoded at 1200 — not invariant under parameter change (C6 violation)
GAP-R2-04: No dual-block disambiguation (DL-016 vulnerable)
GAP-R2-05: CorrectChoice source block is ambiguous — cannot distinguish metadata vs. content block CC
GAP-R2-06: Produces BLOCK enforcement decisions based on potentially phantom DL-008 flags — learner-safety risk if false negatives + P0 risk if false positives trigger unnecessary remediation
remediation_required: UPGRADE-R2-01: Replace findDL008Violations() with Function constructor parse (per Detection Standard section 4.2 reference implementation). The governance guard that BLOCKs certification must use DL-029-immune methodology.
UPGRADE-R2-02: After parsing, extract CorrectChoice and ExplanationWrong[N] from the SAME enclosed object (within-record field extraction per section 4.3).
UPGRADE-R2-03: Add dual-block awareness: when object has both ChoiceA-D (flat, metadata) and Choices.{A,B,C,D} (nested, content), use the nested path for learner-facing verification.
UPGRADE-R2-04: Must pass compliance checks C1-C6 (Detection Standard section 6.1). Specifically, C5: must report 0 DL-008 on Pack B (Function constructor ground truth = 0).

checks.finding: YES — DL-020 fix confirmed applied
checks.detail: extractQuestions() lines 119-129 and extractCases() lines 151-161 both implement the canonical string-aware state machine: inString, stringChar, and escape flags tracked during brace counting. This matches the required state machine in Detection Standard section 4.1.

checks.finding: YES — validateQuestion() accesses fields on the parsed question object q
checks.detail: Line 207-208: val.length > 0 && letter === q.CorrectChoice — extracts CC and EW from the same parsed object. This is the approved within-record methodology. No forward-scan, no window, no regex proximity pairing.

checks.finding: CORRECT — uses within-object field comparison
checks.detail: Line 207-208: if (val.length > 0 && letter === q.CorrectChoice) { this.addError(...) } — CC and EW from same parsed object. Approved within-record methodology per section 4.3.

checks.finding: YES — falls back to new Function() if JSON.parse() fails
checks.detail: extractQuestions() line 140: const fn = new Function('return (' + jsStr + ')'); return fn(); — this is the preferred methodology per section 4.2.

checks.finding: PARTIAL — validates flat fields only, does not check DL-016 mismatch
checks.detail: The validator accesses ExplanationWrongA-D and CorrectChoice from the co-located object. It does NOT compare ChoiceA-D (flat metadata) vs Choices.{A,B,C,D} (nested content) to detect DL-016 contamination. If both exist and differ, the validator EW-vs-CC check is correct but the EW text may describe the wrong topic distractor (DL-016).

checks.finding: CORRECT — skips undefined/null fields, correctly flags empty and non-empty states
checks.detail: Line 199: if (q[field] !== undefined && q[field] !== null) skips absent fields (DL-018). Line 206: skips empty CC slot as correct. Lines 207-208: flag non-empty CC slot as DL-008 error. Correctly handles absent, empty, and non-empty field states.

gaps_found: GAP-EV-01: Does not detect DL-016 (metadata-block ChoiceA-D vs content-block Choices.{A,B,C,D} divergence). EW text may be topically correct for one set of choices but semantically describe a different item distractors.
GAP-EV-02: Does not detect DL-021 pattern (absent non-CC ExplanationWrong fields). Line 199 skips undefined fields without flagging — acceptable for DL-008 but misses DL-021 detection.

GAP-EV-03: Brace-matcher parses entire array in one pass. Object-bounded per-item extraction is not implemented but not required since Function constructor fallback correctly handles all items at once.
remediation_required: ENHANCE-EV-01 (optional): Add DL-016 detection — when object has both ChoiceA-D (flat) and Choices.{A,B,C,D} (nested), compare them and warn if they differ.
ENHANCE-EV-02 (optional): Add DL-021 detection — flag when non-CC ExplanationWrong fields are absent (undefined) rather than empty string.

checks.check: DL-008 detection tests verify within-object field attribution?
checks.finding: NO — all test fixtures use co-located CorrectChoice and ExplanationWrong within small inline JSON strings (~200 chars)
checks.detail: Tests 1-5 (lines 80-125) all test findDL008Violations() with compact JSON where CC and EW are within the same 200-character string. No test verifies behavior when CC appears before QID in the object (Pack B format), or when CC is in a different block than EW, or when the window spans two objects.

checks.finding: NO — zero tests for metadata vs. content block field disambiguation
checks.detail: No test fixture contains BOTH ChoiceA-D (flat metadata fields) AND Choices.{A,B,C,D} (nested content fields). No test verifies that EW text correctly targets the learner-facing choice text.

checks.check: Tests for Pack B CC-before-QID layout (DL-029 mitigation)?
checks.finding: NO — zero test fixtures simulate Pack B CorrectChoice-before-QuestionID serialization order
checks.detail: Detection Standard section 3.1 identifies this as the canonical DL-029 trigger. Without a test for it, the guard cannot verify that its DL-008 detection handles CC-before-QID correctly.

checks.finding: Not applicable — guard uses regex, not brace-matching

checks.check: Cross-check against Function constructor parse ground truth?
checks.finding: NO — zero tests compare regex-scan DL-008 results against Function constructor parse
checks.detail: Detection Standard C4-C5 require cross-checking against Function constructor parse. Pack B ground truth is 0 DL-008 (per section 6.3). No test verifies findDL008Violations() returns 0 on Pack B.

checks.finding: NO — no test varies the +/-1200 window size to verify result stability
checks.detail: The guard uses a hardcoded 1200-character window. Changing this parameter could produce different results — invariance is not verified.

checks.finding: 20 PASS, 0 FAIL — but coverage is methodologically blind to DL-029/016/020
checks.detail: All 20 tests pass because they test the CURRENT algorithm (which has known vulnerabilities). The tests validate the guard does what it claims, not whether what it claims is correct per the Detection Standard.

checks.finding: YES — parseMCQPack() uses inString/stringChar tracking (lines 92-101)
checks.detail: Character-by-character loop tracks inString, stringChar, and escape states during brace counting for per-object extraction. This is string-aware. Compliant with Detection Standard section 4.1.

checks.finding: YES — per-object JSON.parse within brace-matched object boundaries
checks.detail: braceCount tracks {}. When braceCount returns to 0, the object string is JSON.parsed. Each question object is extracted within its own brace boundaries. This avoids the DL-029 cross-object contamination.

checks.finding: YES — evalCaseData() uses inString/strChar tracking (lines 208-252)

checks.check: Case file extraction: Function constructor or eval()?
checks.finding: USES eval() (line 231-232), NOT new Function()
checks.detail: evalCaseData() uses eval(evalScript) where evalScript = globalThis.__tmpArray__ = ... This is NOT the Function constructor (new Function). While eval() works for these files, it is a less safe parsing method and not the Detection Standard preferred approach (section 4.2). The extraction step (finding array boundaries) is string-aware; only the final parse step uses eval().

checks.finding: NO — uses character-position object-boundary extraction, not forward-scan regex
YES — reports per-file question counts in console output for cross-check against grep

gaps_found: GAP-BR-01: Case file extraction uses eval() instead of Function constructor. Low severity — eval() works on current files but Function constructor is preferred per section 4.2.
GAP-BR-02: No DL-008/DL-016/DL-026 detection built in — registry builder extracts metadata only, does not scan for defects.
GAP-BR-03: Does not cross-validate QuestionID count against Function constructor parse ground truth.
remediation_required: ENHANCE-BR-01 (optional): Replace eval() with Function constructor for case file parsing (template: new Function(content + '; return ENHANCED_CASE_BASE;')).

checks.finding: YES — uses content.split('"QuestionID"') to segment blocks, then regex forward-scan within each block for CorrectChoice
checks.detail: Line 9: const blocks = content.split('"QuestionID"'); This splits the file by QID occurrences, then each block is regex-scanned for CorrectChoice. For Pack B (CC before QID), each block STARTS with the item own fields AFTER QID, meaning CorrectChoice from the enclosing object is lost — the forward-scan finds the NEXT item CC at the top of the next block. This produces ~75% false positive rate on Pack B.

checks.finding: NO — raw text split and regex, no string tracking at all
NO — splits by QuestionID delimiter (losing the enclosing object boundary), then regex-scans within text blocks
checks.detail: The split removes "QuestionID" from the file and regroups text between QIDs. If QID appears AFTER CC in the original JSON, the block does not include its own CC — it includes the next item CC. This is a structural impossibility to get correct for Pack B.

gaps_found: GAP-S86-01: QuestionID-split loses object boundaries — CC from different item attributed to current QID (DL-029)
GAP-S86-02: No string-awareness — bracket characters inside string values break block boundaries
GAP-S86-03: Results for Pack B are structurally invalid (~75% false positive rate)
GAP-S86-04: session86_dl026_scan.js additionally uses a second regex match for question_state within the same split block — same vulnerability
remediation_required: REPLACE-S86-01: These scripts should be replaced by the Function constructor scan (reference implementation in Detection Standard section 6.2). The scan_s710r_dl026.js is the approved replacement for dl026_scan.
REPLACE-S86-02: Any report generated from these scripts should be tagged as DL-029 contaminated — results invalid per S725 Detection Standard section 3.1.

checks.finding: YES — line 15: new Function(source + ';\nreturn ' + varName + ';')
checks.detail: This is the approved methodology per Detection Standard section 4.2. The entire array is parsed via Function constructor, then each item is accessed via direct property access on the parsed object.

checks.finding: YES — items are iterated as native objects; all field access is within the same object
checks.detail: For each item, cc = item.CorrectChoice; ewSlot = 'ExplanationWrong' + cc; item[ewSlot]. All from the SAME parsed object. No cross-object attribution possible.

checks.finding: YES — checks for both DL-008 (non-empty EW[CC]) and DL-026 (empty EW[non-CC]) in the same scan pass
checks.detail: Lines 34-39 check DL-008, lines 42-50 check DL-026. Both use within-object field extraction.

checks.finding: PARTIAL — accesses ExplanationWrong fields as direct properties of the merged object; does not separately validate against content-block choices
checks.detail: Packs A/C/D use merged single-object format where both metadata and content fields are co-located. The scan accesses EW fields directly on the parsed object — this is correct for the merged format. However, the scan does not verify that EW text aligns with content-block Choices.{A,B,C,D} (DL-016 guard).

checks.finding: Packs A, C, D only — Pack B and E not included
checks.detail: Line 6: PACKS = ['a', 'c', 'd']; Packs B and E are not scanned. Pack B is known clean (0 DL-008 per Function constructor parse). Pack E has DL-021 (absent fields) rather than DL-026 (empty string fields) — different defect category.

gaps_found: GAP-S710-01: Does not scan Pack B or Pack E. Pack B = 0 DL-008/DL-026 per ground truth — could be added for completeness. Pack E has DL-021 (absent fields) which this scan would flag correctly (undefined = EMPTY_STRING).
GAP-S710-02: Outputs QID lists — good. Each finding includes QID, section, CC, empty slots with details. Compliant with AGENTS.md section 5 (no totals-only reporting).

checks.finding: YES — line 14: new Function(raw + '; return MCQ_BANK_A;')
checks.detail: Approved methodology per Detection Standard section 4.2.

checks.finding: YES — explicitly separates metadata blocks (ExplanationWrong fields) from content blocks (Section + Stem + Choices)
checks.detail: Lines 32-39: distinguishes metadata blocks by presence of ExplanationWrongA fields. Lines 36-38: identifies content blocks by Section + Stem. Lines 64-86: pairs both blocks by QID and records block-level field provenance. This is the canonical dual-block approach described in Detection Standard section 4.4.

checks.finding: YES — topical alignment analysis between EW text and choice text
checks.detail: Lines 114-152: computes keyword overlap ratio between ExplanationWrong[X] text and Choices[X] text. Flags generic/template patterns (line 124-132). Classifies items as DL016_ALL_MISALIGNED, DL016_PARTIAL, DL016_GENERIC, DL026_EMPTY_SLOTS, or CLEAN. This is a sophisticated DL-016 detection implementation.

checks.finding: YES — outputs full per-item JSON inventory with scores
checks.detail: Lines 190: console.log full JSON inventory. Lines 193-203: writes to SESSION805_DL016_INVENTORY.json with per-item details.
